what_the_class_is: The stereo chorus as a whole: the one-pole pre-filter the flanger shares, a chorus voice an output whose modulators the Phase byte sets apart, the balance of dry against wet, then the level and tone stages.

era.when: Mid nineteen-nineties, a custom fixed-point DSP running its effects at 32 kHz with a small control processor beside it.
what_that_implies: A chorus is a delay line whose read address a modulator moves, summed with the dry path; the per-sample cost is one interpolated read a voice and a multiply-accumulate to mix it, so six voices cost six reads and nothing else new.

The modulator is a phase accumulator read through a short shape, and a triangle is the cheapest shape: a folded ramp needs no table. Several voices off one accumulator are that accumulator read at several offsets.

A chorus built after a two-line analogue design feeds each output both lines, one of them inverted, so that the delayed copies cancel in a mono sum; a digital copy of that design costs one more multiply-accumulate an output.
Rates, times and levels are tables indexed by the byte, as the classes that read them closed on; a whole-type model borrows those tables rather than fitting its own.
era.would_be_wrong_if: A reading of the delay's excursion placed the unit's settings outside what either shape predicts by more than the reading's own floor at settings nothing here was built on, or a byte this family reads through a shared table returned values that table does not hold.

candidates.reading: The modulator is a triangle spanning the depth above the pre-delay, and the depth byte is worth the stereo chorus's pitch excursion read as a delay under that shape. The modulator's shape (triangle) and where the pre-filter sits: before the dry and wet paths part, so the dry is filtered too.
candidates.predicts: With the pre-filter switched in the dry path carries the filter as well, so at all-dry the output is the filtered input. Its delay moves at one rate from end to end, so its pitch holds two values a cycle and jumps between them.

candidates.reading: The modulator is a raised sine spanning the depth above the pre-delay, and the depth byte is worth the stereo chorus's pitch excursion read as a delay under that shape. The modulator's shape (raised sine) and where the pre-filter sits: before the dry and wet paths part, so the dry is filtered too.
candidates.predicts: With the pre-filter switched in the dry path carries the filter as well, so at all-dry the output is the filtered input. Its delay lingers at the ends of the sweep and passes the middle quickly, and at every depth its excursion is 0.64 of the triangle's.

candidates.reading: The modulator is a triangle spanning the depth above the pre-delay, and the depth byte is worth the stereo chorus's pitch excursion read as a delay under that shape. The modulator's shape (triangle) and where the pre-filter sits: on the wet path only.
candidates.predicts: With the pre-filter switched in the dry path is untouched, so at all-dry the filter vanishes and at the balance's middle half of the output is unfiltered. Its delay moves at one rate from end to end, so its pitch holds two values a cycle and jumps between them.

what_no_candidate_here_predicts: Whether the chorus's delay line is the one the flanger's loop is around: the front-end claim leaves it open and the two share nothing here but the filter.
What the Phase byte does above 5A, where the page prints nothing: it is held at half a cycle.
Anything at the addresses the page does not print: no node reads them, so every candidate renders them as the power-on state.
